summary.result: Composite analysis results of reanalysis dataset and land surface model simulation revealed that large-scale anticyclonic atmospheric circulation and positive temperature anomalies contribute to increased evapotranspiration and reduced soil moisture, which lead to flash droughts in South Korea.
summary.background: A flash drought is a rapidly evolving drought, unlike general meteorological droughts that develop over months to years due to persistent precipitation deficits.
summary.method: Both the occurrence and duration of flash droughts increased during the analysis period, especially heatwave flash droughts.
